newsitem.title: USA: ISSUER FOCUS - Anaheim, Calif, readies Disney deal.
newsitem.headline: ISSUER FOCUS - Anaheim, Calif, readies Disney deal.

text.p: The City of Anaheim, California plans to come to market in a week with a $518 million bond deal to fund improvements to areas surrounding the Disneyland resort and to the city's convention center.

Under the terms of the deal, Walt Disney Co will partially guarantee payment of the subordinated lease revenue bonds to the bond insurer, and would cover the entire debt if its new project does not open by July 2002, Disney financial adviser Jon Schotz said.
The new project, called "Disney's California Adventure," would be located next to the famed Disneyland theme park.
Anaheim Finance Director William Sweeney said the city plans to hold conference calls with large institutional investors later this week as it prepares for the bond sale.
The bonds are expected to be insured by Financial Security Assurance Inc. They will be sold through negotiation by a syndicate led by PaineWebber Inc around February 4.

The deal will include both taxable and tax-exempt senior lien bonds and subordinated tax-exempt debt. They will be repaid with hotel occupancy taxes, and incremental sales and property taxes generated by the project.
The city said investors in the $518 million deal would have no recourse against the city's general fund, meaning the general fund could not be tapped.
Coming to market with the deal has been a long and difficult process, officials said.
For years, the city has been in discussions with Disney about expanding.
In October, Anaheim's City Council backed Disney's expansion plan. In November, voters approved a local tax measure that will help to support the $518 million bond deal.
